_readme: This is your source list. It is the only file you need to edit.
Buckets starting with an underscore are notes and are skipped by the script.
A plain string   = an RSS feed URL.
An object with   = crawl a sitemap instead, keeping only URLs that
sitemap + match    contain the match text. Use this for sites with no feed.
Marketing Dive's feed path is confirmed. The rest are the standard
published paths for these outlets but I could not verify each one
end-to-end. Expect 2-4 failures on your first run. That is normal and
harmless - the script skips a dead feed and carries on. Check the run
log, delete anything that failed, and move on.
It prints working feed URLs, or the sitemap paths to use instead.
_priority: The boutique bucket is empty and it is the most important one to fill.
Dentsu and Prophet publish for Fortune 500 CMOs - that is not your buyer.
The regional shops competing for mid-market work are the ones whose
content actually sits between you and a sale. Search 3-4 of your money
terms, note who ranks on page one, and add their /feed URLs below.
Almost all of them run WordPress, so <domain>/feed just works.
Eight to twelve of these is worth more than everything else in this file.
_hearst_note: Hearst is several different businesses and you need to pick the right one.
Hearst Bay Area is the marketing-services arm that competes with you;
Hearst Magazines and Hearst newspapers do not. Run discover on
marketing.hearstbayarea.com, then uncomment or replace the line below.
